classification.difficultyReason: Form the triangle containing the longer diagonal, identify the 93-degree angle opposite it and the longer side opposite the requested angle, then use inverse sine and exclude the supplementary result.

content.prompt: The angle between the two sides of a parallelogram is $93^\circ$. If the longer side has length $12\text{ cm}$ and the longer diagonal has length $14\text{ cm}$, find the angle between the long diagonal and the short side of the parallelogram, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$59^\circ$.

Apply the sine rule in the triangle containing the $93^\circ$ angle and the longer diagonal.
answer.worked:
The longer diagonal lies opposite the $93^\circ$ angle in a triangle formed by two adjacent sides. Let $\theta$ be the angle between this diagonal and the shorter side; the side opposite $\theta$ is $12\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{12}&=\frac{\sin93^\circ}{14}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{12\sin93^\circ}{14}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{12\sin93^\circ}{14}\right)\\\theta&\approx58.866859^\circ\\\theta&\approx59^\circ\end{align*}$$

The triangle already has an obtuse angle, so $\theta$ is acute.
